title: Usage signal parity checker and rollback-safe hydrator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We occasionally observe silent divergences between the raw usage events produced by SDKs/agents and the canonical schema consumed by downstream analytics (dashboards, billing, anomaly detection). These divergences manifest as subtle field renames, optional polymorphic payloads, and unhandled nested arrays that cause incorrect aggregation or silent drops during batch backfills. This ticket builds a parity checker service that verifies equivalence between freshly-ingested events and the canonical schema (post-normalization) and a rollback-safe hydrator to perform controlled transformations and backfills. The goal is to detect schema drift early, enable reversible automatic hydration during canarying, and provide a safe dead-letter/backfill flow for historical correction.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Parity checker runs on streaming and batch ingestion paths and reports row-level mismatches to the telemetry dashboard. 2) Hydrator can apply a named transformation profile to incoming events with a feature-flagged canary percentage. 3) Transformations are transactional with an associated rollback plan that can revert hydrated records and re-ingest originals. 4) Dead-letter queue (DLQ) stores non-conforming events with searchable metadata. 5) Metrics: schema rejection rate reduced by 40% within first week of rollout; backfill success >= 99% for corrected cohorts. 6) Post-deployment runbook and automated tests exist in CI.
technical_design: Overview: Build two cooperating components: (A) Parity Checker - a lightweight stream processor that subscribes to the raw ingest topic, applies the canonical normalization pipeline (current runtime normalizer), and compares normalized output to the consumer-facing canonical representation using a deterministic comparator. Emit per-event diff tokens and summary histograms. (B) Rollback-Safe Hydrator - a transformation engine that applies idempotent, versioned hydration profiles to events upstream of the main event topic, logs the original payload to an append-only change store, and supports atomic switches and rollbacks. Key pieces: schema registry integration (schema versions + canonical mapping), comparator library (field-level tolerances, canonicalization hooks), change-store (append-only S3/Parquet partition keyed by tenant and time), DLQ with retention and search index, and control plane flags for canary percent and rollback operations.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 wks): Prototype parity checker as a Flink/Kafka Streams job emitting diffs to telemetry-raw-diffs.* Phase 2 (2 wks): Implement hydrator as a sidecar transformer in the ingest pipeline with feature flags and change-store writes. Phase 3 (1 wk): Integrate DLQ, build simple UI on Console for inspection, and provide CLI tools for rollback. Phase 4 (1 wk): Run controlled canary with internal tenants, validate backfill tools. Phase 5 (1 wk): Full rollout and tidy-up. Deliverables: code in repo 'telemetry/parity-hydrator', infra Terraform for change-store and DLQ, Grafana dashboards, Confluence design doc.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal canary (5% traffic) for 48 hours, monitor parity diff rate and consumer lag. 2) Increase to 20% for one week with daily checks. 3) Open beta for selected external customers. 4) Full traffic after two weeks of stable metrics and sign-off. 5) If parity diffs spike >50% vs baseline or consumer lag increases >100ms P95, automatically toggle to passive mode and notify on-call. 6) Rollback plan documented in runbook with a single-command revert which replays originals from change-store to the canonical topic.
testing_plan: Unit tests for comparator tolerances and normalization rules. Integration tests that spin up local Kafka + test harness to assert parity for positive and negative cases. Chaos tests injecting malformed nested arrays and polymorphic fields. Backfill simulation against archived partitions to validate change-store replay correctness. Canary monitoring includes synthetic events and golden dataset comparisons. All tests run in CI with required coverage gates.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: ingestion_parity_over_time, per-tenant_diff_rate, hydrator_apply_rate, DLQ_volume, change_store_write_errors. Alerts: parity_diff_rate > 0.5% sustained for 30m triggers P1; DLQ growth > 10k/hour triggers P1; change-store write failure rate > 0.1% triggers P2. Alerts route to telemetry-oncall with runbook links.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hydrator introduces latency spikes on hot tenants. Mitigation: use async change-store writes and bounded in-memory buffers; initial canary on low-traffic tenants. Risk: Incorrect rollback could double-count events. Mitigation: record idempotency tokens and implement replay deduplication at consumer layer. Risk: Large DLQ accumulation increases S3 costs. Mitigation: tiered retention and daily compaction jobs.
